Package authentication

Class LoginAttemptLimiter

java.lang.Object
authentication.LoginAttemptLimiter
public class LoginAttemptLimiter extends Object

Title: LoginAttemptLimiter Class

Description: Limits repeated failed logins for TP3 Aspect 5 (Staff log in securely and play the right role, A07 Authentication Failures). After N failed logins in a row for one username, that username is delayed for D: the login page must refuse it, without checking the password, until the delay is over. This implements objective O2.2 of Initial ConOps.pdf and requirement TR-5 of TP3 Testing Requirements.pdf.

The rules are:

  • Only consecutive failures count; a successful login clears the count.
  • The Nth failure starts the delay. The delay covers the half-open interval [start, start + D), so the username is allowed again exactly at start + D.
  • Failures recorded during a delay are ignored, so the delay can never be extended. This guarantees that the only admin can always log in once D has passed (scenario S8).
  • When a delay ends, the username starts again with a fresh set of N attempts.
  • Every username is treated the same whether or not an account exists, so the delay cannot be used to discover which usernames are real. Usernames are compared exactly, as the database does, and null is treated as the empty string.

Time is read from a java.time.Clock passed to the constructor, so tests can control it. The limit and delay are named settings because Aspect 2 (Ronald) will set the final values.

The counts are kept in memory, which suits the single-user desktop application. Whether they should survive an application restart is an open question recorded in Which Aspect and Why.pdf.

  • Constructor Details

    • LoginAttemptLimiter

      public LoginAttemptLimiter()

      Method: LoginAttemptLimiter()

      Description: Creates a limiter with the default limit and delay, using the system clock. This is the constructor the login page uses.

    • LoginAttemptLimiter

      public LoginAttemptLimiter(int maxFailedAttempts, Duration delay, Clock clock)

      Method: LoginAttemptLimiter(int maxFailedAttempts, Duration delay, Clock clock)

      Description: Creates a limiter with the given settings. Settings that would switch the limit off or make it unusable are refused here, so a mistake shows up when the application starts rather than at a login.

      Parameters:
      maxFailedAttempts - the number of consecutive failures, N, that starts a delay; must be at least 1
      delay - how long a delay lasts, D; must be longer than zero
      clock - the source of the current time; tests pass a clock they can move forward
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if N is less than 1, D is missing or not positive, or the clock is missing

  • Method Details

    • recordFailure

      public void recordFailure(String username)

      Method: void recordFailure(String username)

      Description: Records one failed login for a username. The Nth consecutive failure starts a delay of D. A failure recorded while the username is already delayed is ignored, so the delay cannot be extended by repeated guessing.

      Parameters:
      username - the username that was typed; null is treated as the empty string

    • recordSuccess

      public void recordSuccess(String username)

      Method: void recordSuccess(String username)

      Description: Records a successful login, which clears the username's count. The login page only calls this when the username was not delayed.

      Parameters:
      username - the username that logged in; null is treated as the empty string

    • isDelayed

      public boolean isDelayed(String username)

      Method: boolean isDelayed(String username)

      Description: Tells the login page whether a username must be refused right now without checking its password.

      Parameters:
      username - the username that was typed; null is treated as the empty string
      Returns:
      true if the username is inside a delay, otherwise false

    • remainingDelay

      public Duration remainingDelay(String username)

      Method: Duration remainingDelay(String username)

      Description: Returns how long a username must still wait, so the login page can tell the user when to try again.

      Parameters:
      username - the username that was typed; null is treated as the empty string
      Returns:
      the time left in the current delay, or Duration.ZERO if the username is not delayed

    • currentRecord

      private LoginAttemptLimiter.AttemptRecord currentRecord(String key)

      Method: AttemptRecord currentRecord(String key)

      Description: Returns the record for a username, creating it if needed. If the username's delay has ended, the record is replaced by a fresh one, which is how a username gets a new set of N attempts after a delay.

      Parameters:
      key - the username, already converted by key()
      Returns:
      the record to update for this username

    • delayHasEnded

      private boolean delayHasEnded(LoginAttemptLimiter.AttemptRecord record)

      Method: boolean delayHasEnded(AttemptRecord record)

      Description: Tells whether a record had a delay that is now over. This is the one place the end of a delay is decided, so every method agrees on the boundary.

      Parameters:
      record - the record to check; must not be null
      Returns:
      true if the record was delayed and the delay has ended, otherwise false

    • key

      private static String key(String username)

      Method: String key(String username)

      Description: Converts a username to the key used in the map. Null becomes the empty string so a missing username is counted like an empty one and never causes a NullPointerException (CWE-476). Usernames are otherwise kept exactly as typed, because the database compares them exactly.

      Parameters:
      username - the username that was typed
      Returns:
      the key for this username
